diagnosis.statement: A fixed finite backward-history length is dimensional rather than coercive for this critical producer/consumer pair: exact Navier-Stokes parabolic scaling maps the positive-time critical-vorticity separator to any prescribed finite history H while preserving finite I and the weak-L^{3/2} endpoint norm.

failure.scope: Exact smooth whole-space Navier-Stokes solutions on any fixed finite interval [-H,0]. Does not cover genuine ancient solutions on (-infinity,0).
failure.statement: Uniform finite I on a fixed finite backward window does not imply a uniform global L^{3/2,infinity} vorticity-amplitude bound at the endpoint.

gluing_residuals.statement: Scaling maps finite intervals to finite intervals and does not manufacture a mild bounded ancient solution on (-infinity,0).
Any positive interior smoothing lemma remains distinct from a global weak-L^{3/2} vorticity-amplitude theorem without a scale-relative tail/profile-multiplicity certificate.

lesson.statement: Before investing in a proposed finite length/time regularizer for a critical estimate, test whether an exact problem symmetry normalizes that coordinate away while transporting a verified hostile family.

motif.statement: Critical failure scaling lift: if producer and consumer signatures are both invariant under a symmetry, a hostile example at one finite scale can be transported to every finite normalization of the symmetry-dependent coordinate.

obstruction.statement: A successful history-based producer must use a scale-invariant coordinate not removable by finite parabolic rescaling: genuine ancient/backward-sequence structure or an additional scale-relative compactness, frequency, spatial-tail, or profile-tighness certificate.
